target_constraint: Must prevent galvanic corrosion at metal-on-metal interfaces
observed_phenomenon: Modular junction corrosion causing adverse local tissue reaction
mechanism: A ceramic oxide/nitride coating on a metal implant provides a barrier against galvanic corrosion when coupled with other metal components in vivo.
intervention: Apply a zirconium oxide (ZrO₂) or zirconium nitride (ZrN) coating to the titanium alloy femoral stem at the modular junction (e.g., the neck-stem taper interface) to electrically insulate the dissimilar metals and prevent galvanic corrosion.
expected_effect: The coating eliminates direct metal-on-metal contact at the modular junction, preventing galvanic coupling and subsequent corrosion-induced adverse local tissue reactions, while maintaining low friction and wear resistance.
falsification_test: Immerse coated and uncoated titanium alloy modular junctions in simulated body fluid at 37°C for 12 weeks; measure open-circuit potential and corrosion current density via potentiodynamic polarization. If the coated junction shows no significant reduction in corrosion current or if coating delamination exposes bare metal, the intervention fails.
source_spans: "The zirconium oxide or nitride coated prostheses also provide a barrier against implant corrosion caused by galvanic coupling with other metal components or in vivo ionisation of the metal prosthesis."
